register_name: Decision questions: what is known, what is missing, and what would close it
how_to_read_this: Every 'what we have' entry states something this session measured or read on 2026-11-14 and names the official source. Every 'what is missing' entry is a genuine gap: no value is offered where none could be verified. Statuses are: answered (the official source settles it), open-decision (the facts are known, the owner must choose), open-source (a data source the repository does not have is required), probe (a measurement that must be run before the question can be answered at all).

requirements.title: Price-snapshot store: opening and closing numbers for every market originated
Verified results feed, so backtests and ROI can be computed
Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
Publish the model's fair line, the market line, and the difference as separate columns
Separate signal from staking in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers, and publish n with each value
Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper

questions.question: Does the repository hold any opening price at all?
questions.what_we_have: No. data/raw/games.csv has 7,548 rows with 46 columns and carries exactly one price per market. There is no opening column, no timestamp column and no second snapshot. Measured locally on 2026-11-14.
questions.what_is_missing: An opening number, and the time each number was captured.

questions.question: What closing prices does the committed file actually hold?
questions.what_we_have: A closing spread and a closing total on 7,424 of 7,548 games spanning 1999 to 2026, and both moneylines on 5,443. Coverage is complete for every season from 1999 to 2025 and partial for 2026 (148 of 272 games priced).
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing for the closing number itself. The licence and provenance of the file are still unrecorded.

questions.question: Where will opening numbers come from, given no committed source has one?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing committed. The league publishes injury reports, standings, schedules, scores, rosters and Game Books; it does not publish betting prices, and this session found no official league page that does. A price-snapshot store schema is now committed at data/raw/price_snapshots.csv, but it holds zero data rows; it states that no rows will be written until a licensed or permissioned quote source exists.
questions.what_is_missing: A decision on whether to buy or scrape a commercial price feed, or to drop the opening-number half of the requirement.

questions.question: Is the committed results feed complete up to today?
questions.what_we_have: No, not as committed. 137 of the 272 scheduled 2026 games had a kickoff date on or before 2026-11-14; 121 carried a result and 16 did not — the entire Week 9 slate plus the 2026-11-12 Thursday-night game. This session read all 16 outcomes from the league's own schedule pages and proved them: applying them back reconciles 32 of 32 clubs against the official standings on record and points.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing as a measurement. The committed data/raw/games.csv still carries the gap, so the outstanding item is ingestion, not discovery. The 16 rows are written to session-00cf851d/data/verified_results_ingest.csv in the repository's published feed schema.

questions.question: Can any part of the committed results file be shown to agree with the league?
questions.what_we_have: Yes, for two clubs. Recomputed from the file: Pittsburgh 6-2-0, 180 points for, 144 against; Tennessee 1-7-0, 144 for, 199 against. The official standings read on 2026-11-14 give exactly the same figures for both. These are the only two clubs with no game in the missing set, so they are the only two that can be checked.
questions.what_is_missing: The other 30 clubs cannot be reconciled until the 16 missing results are filled.

questions.question: Who owns keeping the results feed current, and on what schedule?
questions.what_we_have: It is currently two rounds stale with no automated refresh and no check that would notice. Nothing in the repository compares played-but-unresulted rows against the count of games the league has finished.
questions.what_is_missing: An owner and a cadence. This is a policy decision, not a data problem.

questions.question: What does 'originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline' actually require of the data?
questions.what_we_have: It requires the model to produce a side number before it is allowed to see any total, and a total before it is allowed to see any moneyline. The committed file supports the ordering because it holds all three markets per game, but it holds them as three finished columns with no record of the order in which anything was produced.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing in the data. The order has to be enforced in code, and no code in the repository enforces it.

questions.question: Must the three markets be produced by three separate models, or one model emitting in a fixed order?
questions.what_we_have: Both are implementable against the committed data. The repository currently has no fitted model of any kind, so neither exists yet.
questions.what_is_missing: A design decision. It changes how a validation gate would attribute a failure.

questions.question: Can the model's fair line be published today?
questions.what_we_have: No. No model in this repository has been fitted and validated, so there is no fair line to print. This session publishes the column with an empty value rather than filling it.
questions.what_is_missing: A model that has passed the validation gates.

questions.question: Can the market line and the difference be published today?
questions.what_we_have: The market line yes, from the committed closing prices. The difference no, because it is the fair line minus the market line and the fair line does not exist. Publishing a difference without a fair line would require inventing one.
questions.what_is_missing: See Q09.

questions.question: What can be published in the difference column honestly, right now?
questions.what_we_have: The market's own error: actual result minus closing price, which needs no model. Across the 121 completed 2026 games the closing spread missed the margin by 9.57 points on average and the total by 10.66 points, with a signed bias of -1.33 points on the spread and +1.00 on the total. n = 121.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing. But note this is a description of the market, not a tradable edge: the closing price is not a price anyone could have taken.

questions.question: How should a leaderboard score signal separately from staking?
questions.what_we_have: The requirement is clear in intent: a strategy that picks well and stakes badly must not outrank one that picks badly and stakes luckily. No scoring rule in the repository separates the two.
questions.what_is_missing: A chosen definition of signal quality that does not depend on stake size.

questions.question: At what sample size does a leaderboard rank mean anything?
questions.what_we_have: Not measured. This session had 121 completed 2026 games available with prices, which is enough to describe the market and not enough to rank a strategy.
questions.what_is_missing: A power calculation run against the real sample size, not an assumed one.

questions.question: Does the league publish a depth chart with 2nd, 3rd and 4th string tiers?
questions.what_we_have: No. The club depth-chart route on nfl.com returns the league's own 404 page. Re-checked independently by this session on 2026-11-14.
questions.what_is_missing: The tier itself. It is not obtainable from the league.

questions.question: Can replacement depth be measured at all from official documents?
questions.what_we_have: Yes, as provenance rather than as a tier. Consecutive official Game Books print four lists: starters, substitutions, did not play and not active. A club that fills a starting slot from the previous week's substitution list has reached less far than one that fills it from the inactive list. This session measured eight replacements across Washington and New York from Week 9 to Week 10: six came from the substitution list and two from the inactive list.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing for the measurement. What is missing is any season-long archive of Game Books, so it cannot yet be computed for more than the games someone retrieves by hand.

questions.question: Does a deep replacement mean the replacement will not produce?
questions.what_we_have: Unknown, and the two available cases point the other way. Both of the Week 10 starters who had been on the previous week's inactive list produced immediately: one rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and caught 3 for 44; the other caught 2 passes for 27 yards. n = 2.
questions.what_is_missing: Sample. Two observations are not a correlation and must not be used as one.

questions.question: What officially sourced numbers exist that a correlation could be computed from?
questions.what_we_have: Official results and official closing prices in the committed file (7,397 games with a result, 7,424 with a closing spread and total), official game-day lineups and inactives from Game Books, official weekly practice and game designations from the injury report, and official standings. All read or measured on 2026-11-14.
questions.what_is_missing: Any historical archive of the injury report. It publishes the current week only, with no per-row timestamp and no back catalogue.

questions.question: What is the largest officially sourced correlation that can be published today?
questions.what_we_have: The relationship between the closing spread and the actual margin: n = 7,397 games, correlation 0.4252, computed this session over every row where both values are present. That is a fact about the market, computed entirely from committed data, with n published.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing for this value. Any correlation involving availability needs a historical injury archive that does not exist here.

questions.question: What minimum n should a published correlation be allowed to have?
questions.what_we_have: The repository's published correlation cells are currently blank, which is the honest state. No minimum has been set.
questions.what_is_missing: A threshold, chosen before any value is computed so it cannot be tuned afterwards.

questions.question: What should send a live strategy back to paper?
questions.what_we_have: The requirement names the mechanism but not the trigger. Two distinct classes of trigger exist and they behave differently: an integrity breach is immediate and needs no statistics, while a performance breach needs a sample size and a threshold before it means anything.
questions.what_is_missing: The thresholds themselves, and a decision on whether a demotion is automatic or reviewed.

questions.question: Is there anything live to demote today?
questions.what_we_have: No. No strategy in this repository has passed its validation gates, so none is eligible to be live and none can be demoted. The gate would currently have nothing to act on.
questions.what_is_missing: A validated strategy, which is the precondition for the gate being testable at all.

questions.question: Is the official injury report usable as a results feed?
questions.what_we_have: No. It publishes practice status and game designation for the current week only, with no per-row timestamp and no outcome column. It is a pre-game input, not a record of what happened.
questions.what_is_missing: Everything a results feed needs. Using this as one would create a look-ahead artifact, because the values are published before kickoff.

questions.question: Why are four clubs missing from the official Week 10 injury report?
questions.what_we_have: Denver, Chicago, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay have no table in the report. All four appear in the official standings with nine games played. The page publishes no reason.
questions.what_is_missing: The reason. It is not published, so it is not recorded here.

questions.question: Is the committed price file's licence and provenance recorded anywhere?
questions.what_we_have: Not by this session. Earlier sessions recorded the same gap and it is still open. The file can be measured but its origin and rights are unknown.
questions.what_is_missing: A provenance and licence decision before the file is used for anything that leaves the repository.

questions.question: Do two official league documents ever disagree about the same player?
questions.what_we_have: Yes. The Week 9 Game Book prints the Giants' starting fullback as 'FB 45 P.Richard'; the Week 10 Game Book prints 'FB 45 P.Ricard' in substitutions. Same club, same number, same position, one week apart.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing. The consequence is recorded: any tracker keyed on surname will count one player as two.

questions.question: Do league game-centre pages reliably publish scores in their server-rendered text?
questions.what_we_have: No. Two of the three game centres this session read returned 'Hidden Score' in every quarter and total cell; the third printed its full line. A scraper would collect nothing from some games and correct values from others, silently.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing. Use the Game Book PDF or the schedule page instead, both of which publish the score as text.
